为全面评估本章提出的人形机器人动态手势唤醒与交互方法的性能，本文选取
了近年来具有代表性的多种视频时空建模或动作检测方案作为对比基线，包括典型
的端到端时空动作检测框架TubeR[15]、STAR[16]、STMixer[17]以及以时序建模为核心
的MFFs[22]、MiniROAD[23]等方法。这些方法大多面向离线视频分析场景设计，在大
规模数据集上取得了较高的动作识别精度，但在边缘设备上的实时性、多用户支持能
力以及工程集成复杂度方面存在差异。
从建模范式上看，TubeR、STAR、STMixer 等方法通常采用端到端的时空特征提
取与动作检测一体化结构，网络深度大、参数规模庞大，对GPU 算力和显存带宽要
求较高；MFFs、MiniROAD 等方法则更多从长时序依赖建模或多模态特征融合（均
依赖于光流计算）角度出发，在提升识别精度的同时，一定程度上牺牲了推理延迟和
工程部署的灵活性，同时无法分辨多人场景。相比之下，本文方法采用“YOLO 实例
追踪+ 轻量化TSM 手势识别”的两阶段架构，在保证识别精度的前提下，显著降低
了模型参数量和单帧推理时间，并通过批量并行推理与ROI 优化策略实现了对多人
交互场景的良好支持。

Online Action Detection (OAD) is the task of identifying actions in streaming videos without access to future frames. Much effort has been devoted to effectively capturing long-range dependencies, with transformers receiving the spotlight for their ability to capture long-range temporal structures. In contrast, RNNs have received less attention lately, due to their lower performance compared to recent methods that utilize transformers. In this paper, we investigate the underlying reasons for the inferior performance of RNNs compared to transformer-based algorithms. Our findings indicate that the discrepancy between training and inference is the primary hindrance to the effective training of RNNs. To address this, we propose applying non-uniform weights to the loss computed at each time step, which allows the RNN model to learn from the predictions made in an environment that better resembles the inference stage. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets, THUMOS, TVSeries, and FineAction demonstrate that a minimal RNN-based model trained with the proposed methodology performs equally or better than the existing best methods with a significant increase in efficiency. The code is available at https://github.com/jbistanbul/MiniROAD.

本模块以唤醒识别模块输出的ROI 区域作为输入，在此基础上采用RetinaFace[48]完
成ROI 内的人脸检测与关键点定位。相较于直接在全幅图像上进行通用目标检测，该
方案能够将计算资源聚焦于交互相关区域，从而更容易在准确率与实时性之间取得
平衡。具体而言，在受限视野与复杂遮挡的交互场景中，ROI 内的人脸检测精度可达
到98.5%，能够较好应对侧脸与局部遮挡等情况；与此同时，得益于对ROI 局部区域
的针对性优化，单帧检测延迟可控制在15ms 以内，满足实时交互需求。随着用户在
机器人前方前后移动，ROI 内的人脸尺度会发生变化，RetinaFace 对多尺度目标的适
应能力能够保持检测稳定性；此外，模型输出的68 个人脸关键点为后续的人脸对齐
与特征提取提供了可靠几何约束，为跨帧追踪与身份关联奠定基础。
3.3.1.2

Though tremendous strides have been made in uncontrolled face detection, accurate and efficient 2D face alignment and 3D face reconstruction in-the-wild remain an open challenge. In this paper, we present a novel single-shot, multi-level face localisation method, named RetinaFace, which unifies face box prediction, 2D facial landmark localisation and 3D vertices regression under one common target: point regression on the image plane. To fill the data gap, we manually annotated five facial landmarks on the WIDER FACE dataset and employed a semi-automatic annotation pipeline to generate 3D vertices for face images from the WIDER FACE, AFLW and FDDB datasets. Based on extra annotations, we propose a mutually beneficial regression target for 3D face reconstruction, that is predicting 3D vertices projected on the image plane constrained by a common 3D topology. The proposed 3D face reconstruction branch can be easily incorporated, without any optimisation difficulty, in parallel with the existing box and 2D landmark regression branches during joint training. Extensive experimental results show that RetinaFace can simultaneously achieve stable face detection, accurate 2D face alignment and robust 3D face reconstruction while being efficient through single-shot inference.

However the citing context also attributes 68 facial landmarks to the model: '模型输出的68 个人脸关键点为后续的人脸对齐与特征提取提供了可靠几何约束'. The identified work's abstract instead states that it manually annotated five facial landmarks: 'we manually annotated five facial landmarks on the WIDER FACE dataset'. This is a quantitative conflict for the attributed landmark count, so the use is contradicted despite the supported detection/localization purpose.

alignment.property: number of facial landmarks/keypoints produced for facial landmark localisation
alignment.scope: RetinaFace's 2D facial landmark localisation output/annotation protocol

review-0.reason: The citing text asserts that RetinaFace outputs 68 facial keypoints for subsequent alignment and feature extraction. The cited RetinaFace abstract states that the work manually annotated five facial landmarks on WIDER FACE and trains 2D landmark regression branches on those annotations, so its landmark localisation uses five landmarks rather than 68. Both assertions concern RetinaFace's facial-landmark localisation output, making the cited value incompatible with the citing attribution.

3.3.1.2

Though tremendous strides have been made in uncontrolled face detection, accurate and efficient 2D face alignment and 3D face reconstruction in-the-wild remain an open challenge. In this paper, we present a novel single-shot, multi-level face localisation method, named RetinaFace, which unifies face box prediction, 2D facial landmark localisation and 3D vertices regression under one common target: point regression on the image plane. To fill the data gap, we manually annotated five facial landmarks on the WIDER FACE dataset and employed a semi-automatic annotation pipeline to generate 3D vertices for face images from the WIDER FACE, AFLW and FDDB datasets. Based on extra annotations, we propose a mutually beneficial regression target for 3D face reconstruction, that is predicting 3D vertices projected on the image plane constrained by a common 3D topology. The proposed 3D face reconstruction branch can be easily incorporated, without any optimisation difficulty, in parallel with the ex

isting box and 2D landmark regression branches during joint training. Extensive experimental results show that RetinaFace can simultaneously achieve stable face detection, accurate 2D face alignment and robust 3D face reconstruction while being efficient through single-shot inference.
